newsitem.title: USA: Rap producer Babyface heads US Grammy nominations.
newsitem.headline: Rap producer Babyface heads US Grammy nominations.

text.p: Rap and pop producer Kenneth "Babyface" Edmonds tied the all-time record for Grammy nominations set by Michael Jackson 14 years ago when he was nominated on Tuesday for 12 of the U.S. music industry's top awards.

The artist, who last year won a Grammy for producer of the year, was nominated in categories ranging from record of the year to song of the year for his work on the "Waiting to Exhale" soundtrack featuring Whitney Houston and Toni Braxton's "Secrets" album.
In one category, best female R&B performance, he was nominated as a producer for four of the five songs.
The pop group Smashing Pumpkins was second in nominations with seven, British singer-songwriter Tracy Chapman and country artist Vince Gill were tied for third with five nominations each.
Tied for fourth with four nominations apiece were rock star Eric Clapton, pop singer Celine Dion, producer David Foster, conductor Pierre Boulez and R&B artist Tony Rich.

The Grammys, the music industry's highest awards, will be presented on Feb. 26 at New York's Madison Square Garden in a three-hour televised show that is expected to be watched by 1.5 billion people in 170 countries, according to the show's producers.
A total of 450 nominations in 89 categories were made public on Tuesday morning at a ceremony attended by several pop stars and New York Mayor Rudolph Giuliani.
